newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bourse to start on-line trading in April.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bourse to start on-line trading in April.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse, the Zagreb Stock Exchange, said on Thursday it hoped to launch a new on-line electronic trading system in April.
"This will technologically enable business to expand, provided there is interest," head of trading Davorin Rusevljan told Reuters.
The new system TEST 1.5 will have a capacity for executing up to 50 transactions per second, he said.
It will be formally presented next week during an international market gathering in Zagreb, the Financial Forum.
"We plan to start with between 10 and 15 brokers at first," Rusevljan said. "For now we have orders from 23 (brokerages), and they will be connected gradually.
The exact day for launching is not yet certain as the state post and telecoms monopoly HPT still has to provide frame relay to brokers.
They are now connected to the bourse via modem and the current screen-based system restricts possibility of expansion.
A typical bourse day sees around 100 deals struck, down from a maximum 164, recorded when business peaked during last autumn's bull run, Rusevljan said.
He said plans are being made for live trading data to eventually be fed on Reuters screens as well.
